eli5.text: The assistant you interact with now runs on a newer version of its underlying model, refreshed by OpenAI in November. If you were comparing responses side by side, you might notice slightly more up-to-date knowledge or reasoning behavior, though most people would just experience it as the same familiar assistant being a bit sharper. This update is live today for everyone using the service.

ai.title: Fast rewrite fallback uses GPT-4o for 16k token limit
ai.summary: Fast rewrite fallback switched from Gemini Flash to GPT-4o via `rewriteWithOpenAI` in `backend/src/fast-rewrite.ts` to support 16k token outputs, addressing Gemini's 8k limit. `common/src/util/file.ts` adds `parseMarkdownCodeBlock` for response parsing. Scope covers backend rewrite logic and common file utilities. `predictedContent` passed to `promptOpenAI` ensures context alignment.

eli5.text: When the assistant tries a fast rewrite using one service and the result looks incomplete, it now retries with a different service that can produce longer answers (up to 16,000 characters instead of 8,000). This means you will see fewer half-finished rewrites when asking for long file changes. A small helper was also added behind the scenes to reliably extract the rewritten code from the response. This is live today.

ai.summary: Fast rewrite backend switches from gpt4o to o3-mini. Cost drops by half with comparable latency and improved accuracy. Change affects backend/src/fast-rewrite.ts only.

eli5.text: When the system rewrites text quickly, it now uses a different helper that costs half as much while producing similar results and slightly better accuracy. Faster rewrites will still come back just as quickly, but they will be generated by this cheaper and more accurate helper. Anyone who relies on the quick rewrite feature will see no change in how they use it, just that it runs more efficiently behind the scenes. The swap is live today.

ai.title: Remove which and where from multiWordCommands
ai.summary: Removed 'which' and 'where' from the multiWordCommands array in backend/src/check-terminal-command.ts. This change prevents these commands from being classified as multi-word commands, altering how they are handled during terminal command checks.

eli5.text: The system that checks what commands you type in the terminal used to treat 'which' and 'where' as special two-word commands. Now it no longer does, so these commands are handled differently, likely as simpler, single-step checks. If you use 'which' or 'where' in your terminal, you'll notice a small shift in how quickly or quietly the system responds, though the end result will still be the same information.

ai.title: Profit margin raised to 0.3
ai.summary: PROFIT_MARGIN constant increased from 0.2 to 0.3 in backend/src/llm-apis/message-cost-tracker.ts. Adjusts internal cost calculation logic. Scope limited to backend cost tracking module.

eli5.text: The hidden fee baked into your AI-powered service just quietly went up. When the system tallies how much it costs to run your chat, it now adds a bigger cushion on top, bumping the internal profit buffer from 20% to 30% of the base cost. You won't see a new button or setting for it; it lives entirely in the backend's bookkeeping and only nudges the final price tag slightly upward over time. This is already in place, so anyone using the service is affected immediately, even if they can't pinpoint where the change came from.

If you read the help articles, you'll see the install troubleshooting page now tells you to try adding sudo to your install command when the setup step fails, as a quick fix before reinstalling your tools. The guide also mentions that it can now work with Google's Gemini model alongside the existing options, so you have more choices for how it thinks through your requests.

ai.title: Prompt agent to accommodate user file edits
ai.summary: main-prompt.ts now partitions addedFiles into updatedFilePaths and newFiles, injecting explicit instruction to accommodate user modifications in read_files tool results. agent-instructions.md clarifies that user edits appear in subsequent read_file results and must be treated as explicit instructions for future write_file operations. Covers backend prompt assembly and system instructions; no CLI/Web surface changes. Updated files are appended after new files in the tool result with dedicated header text.

eli5.text: When you edit a file that the assistant has already read, the assistant now notices your changes instead of working from an outdated copy. The assistant can tell which files you modified versus which it created itself, and it will factor your edits into what it does next. If you looked, you'd see the assistant treating your manual edits as instructions to follow, rather than ignoring them or overwriting them.

ai.title: Extract withCacheControl helper
ai.summary: Added withCacheControl helper to common/src/util/messages.ts to standardize cache_control attachment. Updated backend/src/main-prompt.ts to use this helper instead of inline logic. This refactoring centralizes message transformation logic.

eli5.text: When the assistant responds, it now marks the very last message in a conversation with a special cache-control flag before sending it off. This means the system consistently applies the same caching behavior to the final message, rather than using a different approach each time. If you looked at the conversation flow, you wouldn't notice the messages themselves changing, but the underlying process that prepares them is now more standardized and easier to maintain. This is live today.
